newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET QUIET, RATES STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET QUIET, RATES STABLE.

text.p: HARARE, July 4 (Reutetr) - Trade on Zimbabwe's money market was low on Friday with short-term rates quoted little changed from Thursday's levels, dealers said.

They said the market opened with a Z$80.5 million shortage which was however rectified on maturity of treasury bills, prompting the central Reserve Bank to auction Z$200 million worth of 60-day paper at 24.90 percent.
Treasury bills were being traded on the secondary market at a steady 24.75 percent and call money was at 22 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought steadily at 26.5 percent but sold a touch firmer at 25.25 from 25 percent while bankers acceptance bills were quoted unchanged at 25.5 percent (buying) and at 24.75 (selling).
